title: Declarative agents: what Copilot runs for you, what it needs and where to stop it
summary: The page passes: its controls, licensing distinctions and government-cloud caveats are supported by Microsoft documentation. Minor corrections should clarify the automation mode, acknowledge conflicting hosting and SharePoint licensing guidance, and add missing references.

claims.claim: An administrator blocks an agent in Microsoft 365 admin center through Agents > All agents > agent > Block > Block agent.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. ... select an agent from the list of agents. ... select Block or Unblock. ... select either Block agent or Unblock agent, and then select Save.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks the identified Copilot package.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access controls which users or groups can access agents and plugins.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins. ... Select who can access agents and plugins within your organization.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply a User access baseline once.
claims.quote: Create a new configurationMonitor ... applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode. ... mode ... Optional; defaults to monitorOnly.
claims.fix: Keep the call. Add to the row's note: 'Set the request body's mode to applyOnce; the baseline contains the microsoft.agent.useraccess resource.' The reference is https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta.
